name: High-Frequency Market Microstructure Benchmark: Continuous Double Auction (CDA) vs. Frequent Batch Auction (FBA) Time-Series (Solana/Hyperliquid, Dec 2025)
description: Overview This dataset provides a high-frequency time-series comparison between **Continuous Double Auction (CDA)** and **Frequent Batch Auction (FBA)** market mechanisms. Constructed by simulating both matching engines over 2,678,400 contiguous 1-second intervals (covering the full month of December 2025), the data evaluates execution quality, market depth, price discovery, and operational latency using high-density limit order book (LOB) data from Solana / Hyperliquid. The underlying simulation processed 640,176,812 order-status events across 744 files, executing over 155M SOL (~$20.2B+ USD notional) per market mechanism. Dataset Scale & Specifications Asset: Solana (SOL)Time Horizon: December 2025 (Full Month)Granularity: 1-Second Uniform Intervals ($N = 2,678,400$ intervals per engine)Total Records Processed: 640,176,812 order-status updatesTotal Executed Volume: ~156.3M SOL (FBA) / ~155.6M SOL (CDA)Total Executed Notional: ~$20.31B USD (FBA) / ~$20.20B USD (CDA) Source Dataset Reference: Derived from Hyperliquid order status records (Zenodo: https://zenodo.org/records/18184441). Extension from the work made by: Albers, Jakob (Researcher), Cucuringu, Mihai (Supervisor),Howison, Sam (Supervisor), Shestopaloff, Alexander Y. (Supervisor). Metrics Included The time-series CSVs (`*_timeseries.csv`) capture comprehensive market microstructure and execution quality metrics computed per 1-second interval: 1.
